gap: The hero mock is a DASHBOARD of round summary numbers where the bar is a LEDGER of records, and that single structural choice is what still makes ours read as drawn. The device frame, ground shadow, six named modules, seven complete month labels and the un-severed STAFF ON LEAVE tile all landed, so the r7 crop and skeleton complaints are genuinely closed. What is left is content texture. Wave's accounting fold carries roughly thirty discrete bookkeeping facts: a Select all checkbox, Filter / Sort / Auto updates control pills, four ruled column headers, six dated rows each pairing a merchant (Direct Energy, CALIFORNIA WATER) with an account (Total Checking, Chase Savings, Preferred Credit Card) and a category, an account selector reading $25,980.23, a cursor arrow mid-hover, and a greyed bottom row implying more below. Ours carries five figures and every one is tidy: 48,250 / 18% / 12 / 2 / 5. Not one row, not one client name, not one date, not one document number, and not one interactive affordance anywhere in the frame, no checkbox, caret, filter, input or cursor. The chart makes it worse rather than better: three dashed gridlines carrying no values, no y-axis, flat one-tone bars, so the gridlines are decoration pretending to be measurement. Untidy numbers and dated rows are what read as a record; round numbers and a valueless bar chart are what a designer draws when there is no product behind them. Two secondary faults compound it: both chips assert facts the mock cannot show, the 'Currency billing / Any' tail points into empty beige sidebar rather than at the USD/EUR/AED toggle sitting right there, and 'Languages supported 5' tails into the navy header while the mock contains no language control at all, where Wave's 'Main Street Reno Project' chip names exactly the tag icon it points at. And the mobile fold still carries only a ~120px sliver of navy frame plus one chip, no chart, no modules, no numbers, against Wave's two small but complete and legible callouts. This does NOT require a real capture, and the proof is on our own page 3,000px lower: the 'every market' mock is now fully built out with four Arabic invoice rows (Northwind Trading Co. / 12 مايو 2026 / $4,820.00 / مدفوعة, Harbour Point Ltd / $12,500.00 / متأخرة, Cedar Clinic Group, Studio Meridian), column headers, status pills, a total of $20,320.00 and a real '+ فاتورة جديدة' button. That mock has ledger texture and reads as software; the hero does not. The page's strongest product image is currently the second one, and it is the hero that carries the fold. Rebuild the hero as the invoice or transaction LIST view in that same idiom, dated rows, client names, deliberately untidy amounts, status pills, one filter control and a cursor, and hang the chips off controls that actually exist in the frame.
